title: A Longitudinal Analysis of Public Discourse on AI Ethics in Education Using Twitter Data
subcategory: computational social science: BERTopic + sentiment over time
task: Longitudinal analysis of themes and sentiment in tweets on AI ethics in education
problem: Need an empirical, time-aware account of public discourse on AI ethics in education, especially around the release of ChatGPT.
architecture: BERTopic with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, UMAP and HDBSCAN, with KeyBERT, MMR and LLaMA-based generative topic labels; outliers reassigned and topics reduced to 16; a SetFit classifier (all-mpnet-base-v2 backbone) labels tweet sentiment; monthly sentiment peaks detected and linked to real-world events.
llm_or_encoder: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (topics); all-mpnet-base-v2 SetFit (sentiment); LLaMA for topic labels

datasets.name: Twitter
datasets.details: 14201 English tweets from U.S. users, January 2019 - November 2024

key_results: Initial BERTopic run yielded 57 topics with 6520 (46%) outliers; topics were reduced to 16 after outlier handling.
81.65% of tweets classified positive and 18.35% negative; the SetFit classifier reached 89% accuracy on an 18-tweet validation set.
strengths: Five-year time window covering the pre- and post-ChatGPT period.
Combines topic modelling with event-anchored sentiment peaks.

limitations.text: Twitter-only data from a technically literate user base; engagement-driven ranking may over-represent emotional posts.
Peak detection is sensitive to parameter choices and peak annotation is subjective.
Very high outlier rate (46%) in the initial BERTopic run, and no quantitative topic-quality metric is reported.

notes: Application study from the author-curated corpus.
